title.title: Chromatic quasisymmetric functions are $e$-positive
title.subtitle: Claim: for every natural unit interval graph, each elementary coefficient lies in $\mathbb N[q]$

plain: Count ways to colour a network so linked dots differ: the tally always splits into non-negative pieces

beats.text: A natural unit interval graph on $1, \dots, 5$: each vertex sees an interval of others
Its chromatic quasisymmetric function counts proper colourings, graded by $q$
The claim: every $e$-coefficient is a polynomial in $q$ with nonnegative integer coefficients

steps: Match each coefficient with the counting series of an algebra
A count is never negative, so each coefficient is positive
Bijections then give each allowed ordering its own partition

achievement.label: Shareshian–Wachs conjecture (2016), the positivity half
achievement.context: The $q = 1$ case, Stanley–Stembridge, was proved by Hikita in 2024
achievement.note: $e$-unimodality, the other half of the conjecture, is untouched

verify.detail: The full identity, stated as a witness structure, so no theorem name is listed
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Colour the vertices so neighbours differ. This function counts every way, graded by q.
Each coefficient is matched to a count, and counts are never negative.
Claimed: every coefficient is a positive polynomial.

sources.quote: The q=1 case (Stanley–Stembridge) was already proved by Hikita in 2024
which is why the lean table lists no theorem_names
